correctness.rationale: Directly enumerated 234 4-arcs and, independently, 234 smooth quadratic forms; both produce exactly 4,641 distinct conic-pair concepts, 78 forbidden seven-sets and the complete VC face polynomial. Two independently written programs perform all \(3^{13}\) partial-assignment transitions and give Littlestone depth exactly eight. One constructs and directly rechecks all 256 feasible leaves of an explicit complete depth-eight tree, while exhaustive DP forbids depth nine. The 78 forbidden seven-sets have pairwise intersection at most five, establishing basis exchange and a rank-seven sparse-paving matroid. Classical matroid shellability and reduced Euler characteristic 714 establish the integral wedge-of-714-six-spheres conclusion. Binary boundary rank 924 was independently checked. No finite observation was extrapolated to unbounded field sizes.

originality.rationale: Distinct from the already known ordinary two-conic VC polynomial: the exact new online dimension is 8, proved by independent exhaustive ternary dynamic programs and a complete 256-leaf tree. The resulting rank-seven sparse-paving matroid and its 714-sphere integral homotopy type are structurally identified, not simply restated from the prior static census. Closest published conic-pair and blocking-set classifications were compared by implications. Full text of one plausible blocking paper remains inaccessible, but no available statement decisively covers the new adaptive result.

value.rationale: Exact online learnability is a natural invariant not fixed by the pre-existing static VC census; the sharp eight-versus-seven gap and a 256-leaf adaptive witness are substantive. The sparse-paving matroid interpretation gives a structural explanation for the 78 incidence obstructions and turns their exact counts into a nontrivial integral homotopy classification. This connects three independently motivated theories (finite conic incidence, mistake-tree learning, matroid topology); the result is not an arbitrary numerical slice or a routine recoding of a known table.
